assets.title: The No-Village 14-Day Guide
assets.content:
# The No-Village C-Section
*First 14 days alone with a newborn after major abdominal surgery - survival and function, no village required.*

## Who this is for

You came home from a C-section without a mother, auntie, or cousin installed in your guest room. Maybe your partner got two weeks off, maybe five days, maybe none. Everyone online says "accept help" - but there is no help standing in your kitchen. This guide assumes **nobody is coming**, and builds your first 14 days anyway.

## The one fact that organizes everything

A C-section is major abdominal surgery. You are a surgical patient carrying a newborn. Every instruction below flows from that: protect the incision, move gently but move, and lower the bar for everything that is not baby + healing.

## Your 14-day map

**Days 1-3 (survive):** pain on schedule, not on courage. Walk short loops. Everything within arm's reach.
**Days 4-7 (function):** shower normally, short walks outside, one "win task" per day max.
**Days 8-14 (rhythm):** light routine returns; still nothing heavier than the baby.

## Pain management (the honest version)

- Paracetamol (acetaminophen) and ibuprofen are the standard pair and are considered compatible with breastfeeding - take them ON SCHEDULE the first week, before pain spikes, exactly as your surgeon prescribed.
- Pain that arrives late "because I'm tough" costs you sleep, mobility, and healing.
- A pillow pressed to your belly when coughing, sneezing, laughing, or rolling changes everything.

## Moving safely

- Rolling out of bed: drop legs first, push up with arms ("log roll").
- Walk every few hours, even just kitchen-to-sofa - walking prevents clots.
- Nothing heavier than the baby for ~2 weeks; nothing heavier than ~10-15 lb / 6 kg until your 6-week review says otherwise.
- No driving until you can brake hard without hesitating (commonly around 2 weeks; your clinician decides).
- No baths/swimming until your clinician confirms healed (showers fine).

## Incision care

Shower water over it is fine; mild soap, pat dry, no scrubbing, no creams/pastes/herbs on it. Air + time heals. Watch it daily with the Decision Card.

## Feeding the machine (you)

You heal on food and water, not on leftovers. One-handed meals count. Protein + water at every chance. If appetite vanished: small, often.

## The no-village systems

1. **The Landing Zone:** one chair/bed corner with 48 hours of supplies - water bottle, snacks, chargers, nappies, wipes, muslins. Baby changes happen there.
2. **The One-Trip Rule:** never climb stairs or cross the house for one item. Carry a basket.
3. **The 15-Minute Visitor:** anyone who visits brings food or holds the baby WHILE YOU SHOWER - then goes home. Script Pack has the words.
4. **Delivery apps > hero cooking.** This is the two weeks it's worth it.

## What "normal" feels like

Sore incision improving daily, bleeding like a heavy period fading over weeks, afterpains while breastfeeding, exhaustion that sleep partially fixes, weepy "baby blues" easing after two weeks. None of that is failure.

*Sources: Mayo Clinic C-section recovery guidance; Cleveland Clinic recovery timeline (2021); WebMD post-C-section recovery & warning signs; Medical News Today wound-infection review. Educational only - your own clinician overrides this guide.*

assets.title: Daily Survival Checklist Days 1-14
assets.content:
# Daily Survival Checklist (Days 1-14)
*One tick list. Survive first, function second.*

## Morning (10 minutes)
- [ ] Pain meds taken (on schedule, not on pain)
- [ ] Water bottle filled - it lives next to you now
- [ ] Incision peeked at (photo every 2 days)
- [ ] Today has ONE goal only. Name it: ____________

## Movement (every few hours)
- [ ] Walked a loop (bed -> kitchen counts on Days 1-3)
- [ ] Did the log-roll getting up, pillow-hug when sneezing/coughing
- [ ] 3 deep breaths, 10 shoulder rolls hourly

## Lifting rules (non-negotiable)
- [ ] Lifted nothing heavier than the baby
- [ ] Toddler/older child: sit-down cuddles only, no lifting
- [ ] Asked for/delivered help with anything heavier

## Evening reset (15 minutes)
- [ ] Tomorrow's Landing Zone restocked: water, snacks, nappies, wipes, charger
- [ ] Fed yourself actual food today? If not: note why, fix tomorrow
- [ ] One-line log: pain __/10 . walked? Y/N . incision normal? Y/N

## Week 2 additions (Days 8-14)
- [ ] One short outdoor walk daily
- [ ] Booked/attended the ~2-week postnatal check
- [ ] Brake-test question if driving is near: can I slam the brakes without thinking twice?

assets.title: The Incision Decision Card
assets.content:
# The Incision Decision Card
*Look at the incision + how you feel. One pass. Act on what you find.*

## 1 - Is ANY of these true right now?

- Fever **38C / 100.4F or higher**, or chills/shivering
- Incision: red spreading outward, hot, swollen, opening, or leaking pus / bad-smelling fluid
- Pain that is **getting worse** instead of better after day 3-4
- Vaginal bleeding soaking a pad per hour, large clots, or foul smell
- Calf pain/swelling/heat on one leg, chest pain, or shortness of breath
- Severe headache that will not shift, or vision changes

-> **ANY ONE = contact your clinician TODAY. Fever + any incision sign = same hour. Chest pain/breathlessness/calf signs = emergency now (clot until proven otherwise).**

## 2 - None of those, but worried about looks?

| Seeing | Meaning | Do |
|---|---|---|
| Slight redness thin line, mild swelling days 1-3 | Normal healing | Routine continues |
| Pink/purple fading scar line weeks later | Normal maturing | Routine continues |
| Small clear fluid seep after activity | Borderline | Photo today + tomorrow; call clinic if it repeats/worsens |
| Hard lump at one end | Watch | Mention at week-2 check; photo log |
| Weeping past day 5 / reopening edges | Not normal | Clinic today |
| Numbness around incision | Very common | Normal for months |

## 3 - The mood check (30 seconds)

Beyond two weeks of weepy blues -> or any moment of "I can't do this," hopelessness, thoughts of harming yourself or the baby -> **this is medical, not moral.** Contact your clinician and use the crisis lines on your Rescue Card. Screens route; they never diagnose.

## 4 - Someone touched the incision / applied something

Herbs, pastes, belly-binding over an unhealed wound: rinse gently with clean water if freshly applied, photograph, run section 1, use the reset script, log it.

assets.title: No-Village Scripts
assets.content:
[[SCRIPTS]]
TITLE: No-Village Scripts
SUB: You are not superwoman and you don't owe anyone the performance of coping.
SCRIPT: The visitor who sits down expecting tea | So glad you came - you're actually perfect timing. Hold him while I grab a shower, then I'll walk you out, I'm on painkillers schedule." ((They held the baby. You showered. Fifteen minutes, dignity intact.))
SCRIPT: Declining the trip/event in week 2 | Recovery from the surgery isn't there yet - doctor says no long trips this fortnight. We'll be there properly once I'm cleared at my check-up.
SCRIPT: Asking for REAL help (specific asks work) | If you want to help us this week, here's exactly what would change our lives: Tuesday groceries, Wednesday laundry pickup, Friday a pot of soup. Pick one?
SCRIPT: Partner back at work after five paternity days | We need to plan your week like a rota: nights are split, mornings you handle [task] before leaving, weekends we trade shifts so I sleep in. This is two more weeks, then we renegotiate.
SCRIPT: Long-distance village (the diaspora special) | Group chat message: "We're doing meal-drop deliveries instead of visits: Tue/Thu/Sun slots open. Address to send courier: [x]. Thank you - this is the village, remote edition.
SCRIPT: "My mother would have come if she could" grief moment | Say it out loud to yourself: *"She couldn't come. I am allowed to find my own way. Look what I did today anyway."*
SCRIPT: When baby blues turn dark (say this to someone) | I'm not okay. This feels beyond tired. Can you come sit with me / can I call you tonight?" - and book the clinician line. You would never judge a friend for this.
[[/SCRIPTS]]

assets.title: Bad-Day Rescue Card + crisis lines
assets.content:
[[RESCUE]]
TITLE: Bad-Day Rescue Card
*For the day everything goes wrong. It happens. Here's the reset.*

## The rule of the bad day

A bad day is not a failed recovery. Surgical healing is not linear. Today we drop to MINIMUM MODE and tomorrow restarts - no debt, no guilt.

## Minimum Mode (the only 5 things)

1. Meds on schedule
2. Baby fed somehow (breast/bottle/expressed - all count)
3. You ate ONE real thing and drank water
4. Incision glance + red-flag scan
5. Everyone alive -> day counted as survived

Everything else - laundry, visitors, the perfect routine - waits.

## Common bad days -> instant moves

**"I overdid it and I'm wrecked"** -> Cancel tomorrow's goal. Meds, comfort, horizontal. Healing happens lying down.

**"Incision popped a sting / bled a dot after lifting"** -> Photo, pressure 10 min, Decision Card scan. No repeat lift. Call clinic if reopened/oozing.

**"Nobody checked on me today"** -> Send Script 5 to the group chat NOW. State the specific ask. People genuinely don't know.

**"I cried all afternoon"** -> Hydrate, eat, tell one human by voice/text. Two weeks+ of this = clinician call. Crisis numbers below.

**"I resent the baby" (fleeting horror thought)** -> Extremely common, not a verdict on you. Sleep-deprived brains say wild things. If persistent/darkening -> clinician, today-tomorrow.

## Numbers that answer 24/7

Nigeria: Emergency **112** . SURPIN +234 806 210 6493 . MANI 0809 111 6264
UK: Emergency **999** . Samaritans **116 123**
US: Emergency **911** . Crisis **988** . Canada: 911 / 988

*Educational support - not diagnosis. Your clinician overrides everything here.*
EMERG: Nigeria 112 | 112
EMERG: UK 999 | 999
EMERG: US 911 | 911
EMERG: US 988 | 988
[[/RESCUE]]
